Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old man with several weeks of intermittent headaches, episodic palpitations/tachycardia, shortness of breath, bilateral arm tingling, decreased appetite with 5 lb unintentional weight loss, and reduced libido since changing jobs; has history of hyperthyroidism treated with thyroxine — clinic examination and thyroid blood tests planned.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Intermittent severe headaches, episodic palpitations, shortness of breath, bilateral arm tingling, reduced appetite with 5 lb weight loss, and decreased libido.
- Timeline:
  - Symptoms began roughly when patient changed jobs (timeframe described as "since I changed my job"); headaches and other symptoms occur intermittently and "come and go."
  - Weight loss approximately 5 pounds, unintentional; duration same as other symptoms.
  - Palpitations occur about once daily (may be more).
  - Reduced libido started around same time as job change.
- Symptom characteristics and progression:
  - Headaches:
    - Occur mostly during work hours (in meetings or sitting at computer).
    - Located primarily in the front of the head.
    - Associated with mild nausea.
    - Not previously a problem before job change.
  - Palpitations/fast heartbeat:
    - Occur approximately once per day or possibly more.
    - Patient notes "heart is beating kinda fast."
  - Shortness of breath:
    - Occurs while sitting at desk; not with exercise.
    - Patient related this to the "feeling hot" entry in the record.
  - Paresthesia:
    - Tingling in both arms/hands described as "quick pricking."
    - Not present in legs.
  - Appetite/weight/libido:
    - Reduced appetite, unintentional 5 lb weight loss.
    - Decreased libido since job change.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Symptoms occur primarily at work; do not report clear relieving factors.
  - Stress at work rated 7–8/10 and noted as high-pressure environment.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - Nausea with headaches.
  - No leg paresthesias.
  - No exercise-related shortness of breath.
  - No recreational drug use reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No prior history of frequent headaches before job change.
  - Denies smoking.
  - Denies recreational drug use.
  - Drinks alcohol about once per week (a couple of glasses of wine).
  - No other medical problems reported besides hyperthyroidism.

Past Medical History:
- Hyperthyroidism:
  - On thyroxine; patient reports taking medication as prescribed. (dose/route/frequency not documented)
  - No further details provided about duration, cause, prior treatments, or complications.

Medications:
- Thyroxine — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- No allergies reported (patient did not report any when asked).

Social History:
- Occupation: Lawyer in London; recently changed jobs.
- Work environment: Mix of meetings and prolonged computer reading; symptoms mainly occur at work.
- Stress: Reports current stress level 7–8/10; endorses chronic high-pressure environment in law firm.
- Alcohol: Drinks approximately once weekly, a couple of glasses of wine.
- Tobacco: Denies smoking.
- Recreational drugs: Denies use; reports never used cocaine or marijuana.
- Living/financial factors: None discussed.

Family History:
- Not discussed / no family history provided.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not provided in transcript.
- Examination findings: None documented in consultation; in-person exam planned (cardiac and respiratory to be assessed).

Investigations:
- Planned:
  - Blood tests for thyroxine / thyroid function (specific tests not enumerated).
- No investigations or imaging results available from this visit.
- No ECG or other tests performed or ordered explicitly in the transcript beyond thyroid blood tests.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Intermittent headaches with associated nausea
  - Assessment: New-onset intermittent frontal headaches, temporally associated with work and increased stress since job change.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange in-person clinic visit for examination.
    - Perform clinical assessment in clinic; further investigations to be determined after examination.
    - No new medications started at this remote consult.
- Issue 2: Episodic palpitations and shortness of breath
  - Assessment: Episodic palpitations (approximately daily) and exertion-independent shortness of breath occurring predominantly at desk/work; possible relation to thyroid status or anxiety/stress — assessment pending in-person evaluation.
  - Plan:
    - In-person cardiac and respiratory examination in clinic.
    - Perform thyroid function blood tests (to assess for thyroxine adequacy or thyroid dysfunction).
    - Further testing (e.g., ECG, ambulatory monitoring) to be considered based on clinic exam and blood results — not explicitly ordered at this consult.
- Issue 3: Bilateral arm tingling (paresthesias)
  - Assessment: New bilateral upper extremity tingling described as "quick pricking," episodic, not associated with leg symptoms; etiology undetermined from remote consult.
  - Plan:
    - Evaluate neurologic and musculoskeletal causes during in-person exam.
    - Consider further investigations if abnormal exam findings (not specified at this visit).
- Issue 4: Reduced appetite, unintentional weight loss (5 lb), decreased libido
  - Assessment: Unintentional weight loss and decreased libido temporally associated with job change and other systemic symptoms; possible contributors include thyroid dysfunction, stress, or other medical causes.
  - Plan:
    - Include weight check and focused history/physical in clinic.
    - Review thyroid function (blood tests ordered as above).
    - Address psychosocial/stress factors and consider referral or support depending on findings.
- Issue 5: Known hyperthyroidism on thyroxine
  - Assessment: History of hyperthyroidism treated with thyroxine; patient reports adherence.
  - Plan:
    - Check thyroid function tests to assess adequacy of replacement/management.
    - Review thyroxine dose and adherence during in-person visit; adjust management only after results/assessment.
- General plan items:
  - Patient to book an in-person clinic appointment (can book via the app) to see a clinician for physical examination (cardiac and respiratory exam emphasized).
  - Blood tests for thyroid function to be performed.
  - No new medications to be prescribed until after in-person assessment and test results.
  - Physician will communicate findings to clinic staff so patient does not need to repeat full history at appointment.
  - Follow-up plan contingent on exam and laboratory results.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, temperature, oxygen saturation) not provided.
  - No physical examination findings documented (in-person exam planned but not yet performed).
  - No thyroid function test results available.
  - Thyroxine dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - No medication list beyond thyroxine; reconciliation not completed.
  - No family history provided.
  - No ECG or other cardiac investigations documented; ambulatory monitoring not addressed.
  - Lack of specific symptom onset date (only “since job change”) and duration in exact time units.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Clinic record reportedly states "feeling hot," but patient did not explicitly endorse feeling hot; patient instead described shortness of breath. Conflict noted between recorded "feeling hot" and the patient's verbal report emphasizing shortness of breath.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall audio/text intelligible with occasional pauses and brief silences; clinician and patient statements are generally clear. Minor conversational interruptions and filler words present but do not prevent extraction of clinical information.
